1. Background and Context

Tamil Nadu is one of the most water stressed State in India due to its unique hydroclimatic, geographic, and demographic characteristics. The State accounts for nearly 4% of the country’s population but has access to only about 3% of India’s water resources. Unlike many other States, Tamil Nadu is largely dependent on monsoon rainfall and has no _ perennial river originating within its territory.

The Water Resources Department, Government of Tamil Nadu, is entrusted with the Planning, Development, Operation, and Maintenance of water resources across the State. The Department manages 17 major river basins, 90 reservoirs, more than 14,307 irrigation tanks, and an extensive network of approximately 46,000 km of irrigation channels, in addition to floodplains, supply channels, and catchment areas that are critical for irrigation, drinking water supply, and flood moderation. -

Ground water plays a critical supplementary role, especially during deficit rainfall years. However, large parts of the State have been classified as over-exploited or critical, indicating unsustainable extraction patterns. Per capita water availability in Tamil Nadu is significantly lower than the national average and is projected to decline further, placing the State in the category of water-scarce regions.

Over the past several decades, these vital water bodies have been severely affected by the unchecked proliferation of Prosopis juliflora (locally known as Seemai Karuvelam), an invasive alien species. Its aggressive growth has resulted in large scale _ ecological degradation, loss of hydraulic efficiency, and diminished water storage capacity, posing a serious threat to water security and climate resilience in Tamil Nadu.

The objective of the scheme is to promote skill development of the beneficiaries by imparting practical training on mulberry cultivation and modern sericulture techniques. By imparting skill upgradation training to sericulture farmers, the productivity can be increased. During the year 2024-2025, a sum of Rs.164.50 lakh has been sanctioned for providing training to 2350 sericulture farmers.

4.4. Support for establishment of Chawkie Rearing Centres

‘Chawkie’ refers to 7 days old young-age silkworms from hatching to second moult and the centres which are specialised in rearing of chawkie worms are called as ‘Chawkie Rearing Centres’. Farmers / entrepreneurs are supported to establish Chawkie Rearing Centres to ensure continuous

4.5. Support for establishment of Silk Reeling Units

Silk reeling sector plays a significant role in the growth and stability of Sericulture industry and also in converting the cocoons into high quality yarn required for textile production.

Multi-end silk reeling units and Automatic silk reeling units are an expression of modernized silk reeling techniques. Introduction of these modernized units have resulted in tremendous increase in the productivity of silk reeling industry.

To encourage youth and entrepreneurs to establish improved silk reeling units and to increase silk production in the State, financial assistance is provided for the following components:

Tamil Nadu, being a leading State in the production of bivoltine silk, has carved a niche for itself in the field of handloom weaving through its artistic designs of traditional silk sarees of Kancheepuram, Arni, Kumbakonam, Thirubuvanam and Sirumugai and Salem Bivoltine Silk Dhoties.

To attain self sufficiency in silk production, the Government is continuously supporting the farmers and entrepreneurs to practice silkworm rearing and silk reeling. Continuous support from the Government, technological innovations and growing global demand are the key factors in driving the growth of Tamil Nadu Sericulture industry.

5

4. Welfare Schemes of the Department

The contribution of sericulture farmers and silk reeling entrepreneurs is vital for the growth of Sericulture sector in the State. Various beneficiary oriented development schemes are being implemented by the Department under State Plan and Silk Samagra-2 schemes to encourage the participation of stakeholders in Sericulture sector and to improve their socio-economic status by promoting seed production, pre and post cocoon production levels.

India as well as Tamil Nadu aims to promote growth and development of the silk industry through “SILK SAMAGRA-2”, by attaining the following goals:

 Provide financial assistance to sericulture farmers and silk entrepreneurs

 Enhance the productivity and quality of silk production

 Promote the use of modern technology and machinery in silk production

6

 Develop infrastructure for silk production and marketing

 Promote the export of silk products

During the year 2025-2026, the State Government has allocated a sum of Rs.4027.75 lakh for the implementation of welfare schemes. Further, to implement the welfare schemes under Silk Samagra-2 during the year 2025-2026, the Central Silk Board has approved to sanction a sum of Rs.5014.00 lakh as Government of India’s share.

4.1. Support for Development of Mulberry Nursery

Assistance is provided for establishment of ‘Mulberry Nursery’ to produce and supply quality mulberry saplings to the farmers who are all newly planting mulberry. During the year 2024-2025, financial assistance of Rs.46.13 lakh has been provided to 54 farmers for raising mulberry saplings in 40 acre.

7

4.2. Package of Assistance for Silkworm Rearing

Silkworm rearing requires well established and maintained mulberry garden to feed quality leaves to silkworm and properly built separate rearing sheds to maintain optimum microclimate required for silkworms.

To reduce the drudgery in mulberry garden maintenance and silkworm rearing, farm mechanisation is encouraged through usage of improved silkworm rearing appliances and farm equipments. For successful cocoon harvest and better productivity, farmers need to adopt recommended prophylactic measures.

The Hon'ble Minister (MS&ME) has made the following announcement during the financial year 2024 - 2025:-

“A special seed fund in the form of a grant will be introduced for startups run by differently-abled individuals and transgender people in order to achieve inclusive growth in new-age entrepreneurship development”.

2. Based on the above announcement, the Mission Director/Chief Executive Officer, TANSIM has stated that the Special Seed Grant is designed to support the early-stage financing needs of Differently Abled and transgender individuals. This fund, in the form of grants, aims to bridge the financial gap from concept to commercialization, including patentable ideas. The Grant will also provide support for the Idea-to-POC (Proof of Concept) stages, covering pre-startup activities by offering crucial early-stage financial assistance to deserving ideas or technologies. This grant is intended to support the prototyping and testing of innovative concepts by early-stage startups, who are differently abled or transgender. Recognizing the unique challenges faced by transgender

2

innovators, the program adopts a slightly more flexible approach to eligibility criteria to encourage their participation.

I, Grant Highlights

The Granting provided under this program will be upto a maximum of Rs. 5.00 Lakh, subject to the approval of the TANSIM High-Level Committee. The Special Seed Grant is focused on providing early-stage financial support to differently abled and transgender founders for their indigenous ideas, business and technologies, enabling up-scaling and related activities. The Grants will be disbursed to deserving startups following proper due diligence.

II. Areas covered under the Grant

The Special Seed Grant aims to provide early-stage financing for startups led by differently-abled and transgender individuals, facilitating their transition from concept to commercialization.

III. Definition of a Startup A Startup is a registered entity that meets the following criteria:

a. Incorporated as a Private Limited Company, Registered Partnership Firm, or Limited Liability Partnership (LLP).

b. The entity must be less than 10 years old from the date of incorporation.

c. The entity's annual turnover must not exceed INR 50 crore in any financial year since incorporation.

4.2.2 Water Supply

Town Panchayats are taking various efforts

to provide protected water supply to all

households in their jurisdiction. These include

regulating the water supply, ensuring the

provision of prescribed quantity of water to all,

augmentation of additional water sources,

construction of overhead tanks for sufficient

storage, replacing the damaged pumping main

245

supply pipelines in Town Panchayats.

In all Town Panchayats, water is supplied to the public at the rate of 70 litre per capita per day (LPCD), while in Town Panchayats with Under Ground Sewerage Systems (UGSS), action is being taken to provide water supply at the rate of 135 liters per person per day. Out of the total 487 Town Panchayats, 325 are supplied with drinking water through the Combined Water Supply Schemes maintained by TWAD Board. The remaining Town Panchayats provide water supply through local sources. Currently, 42% of households have their household water connections. The goal is to provide functional household tap connections to all households, ensuring universal access to drinking water.

Key activities of Town Panchayats include augmenting and maintaining water sources, restoring ponds and wells, reusing of recycled treated water and also establishment of new rainwater harvesting arrangements and restoration of existing rain water harvesting structures etc., in all types of buildings through

community contributions are important for achieving sustainable water economics.

Major water-related reforms envisaged in Town Panchayats include accessing 20% of water requirements from treated and recycled water, reduction of non revenue water below 20% and restoring water bodies.
